summary: The Independent explains the history and customs of American Thanksgiving, a national holiday on the fourth Thursday of November (23 November in 2023). It traces the holiday to early feasts in 1619 and 1621 and to Lincoln's 1863 proclamation, and describes modern traditions such as food, football and the Macy's parade. It also covers the controversy over the holiday's treatment of Native Americans and how other countries observe their own Thanksgivings.
one_line: An explainer on Thanksgiving's origins, traditions, controversies and food, from the 1621 Plymouth feast to Lincoln's 1863 proclamation and the Macy's parade.
key_facts: Thanksgiving is a US national holiday celebrated every fourth Thursday in November; in 2023 it fell on Thursday 23 November.
The holiday honours the 'first' Thanksgivings in America, in 1619 in Virginia and in 1621 in Plymouth, Massachusetts.
In 1621 colonists in Plymouth, later known as the Pilgrims, allegedly shared a meal with the Wampanoag Indians, which lasted three days.
The 1621 feast honoured the help the Pilgrims received from Native Americans in cultivating crops and surviving their first harsh winter.
George Washington, John Adams and James Madison each called for days of thanks during their presidencies.
In 1863, during the Civil War, President Abraham Lincoln declared a national Thanksgiving Day to be held each November.
Thanksgiving has become a mostly secular holiday centred on food, family and football, with multiple NFL teams playing on the day.
The Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade in New York City is described as the world's largest Thanksgiving parade, with giant cartoon balloons, marching bands and dancers.
Black Friday follows Thanksgiving and kicks off the month-long shopping season for the winter holidays.
Some Americans view Thanksgiving as a celebration of the conquest of Native Americans and their lands, and ignore it or observe a National day of Mourning instead.
Canada celebrates Thanksgiving on the second Monday in October, and Liberia on the first Thursday of November.
An estimated 46m turkeys are killed annually for the holiday, while the president pardons two turkeys each year.
Typical Thanksgiving foods include turkey, yams topped with marshmallows, stuffing, cranberry sauce, cornbread and pumpkin pie, with vegan and vegetarian options available.
